note: Llama 2 7B Q4_0 (llama-bench tg128) and Blender Open Data (three-scene sum) results that fill matrix cells of the comparison chips; every value with the URL it was read from. id = position in this list, used by mxfill.py. LLM x is tokens/s (tg128), Blender median_spm is the median over runs of the per-run sum of the monster, junkshop and classroom scenes in samples per minute (x = median_spm/60), the method of x86.py and nv2.py. No row carries power: mxfill.py borrows it from rows already on the page.

rows.device: NVIDIA RTX Spark N1X (6144-core Blackwell RTX GPU)

Version check in the same snapshot: OptiX medians in 5.3.0 run above 4.5.0 by 13% for the RTX 5090 Laptop (8943.17 over 5 runs vs 7887.03) and 28% for the RTX 5090 (19202.05 over 17 vs 14965.98), so this point may sit high against the 4.5.0 points.
Its only GPU run in Open Data. The device name "Intel(R) Graphics" is shared by many Intel chips, so the run was matched by its CPU name.

gaps.llm|Intel Core Ultra 7 155H: No Llama 2 7B Q4_0 tg128 run that names this chip was found. The SYCL docs of llama.cpp (docs/backend/SYCL.md) give "MTL 16 tokens/s" for this model, with neither the SKU nor the test named; the Vulkan scoreboard has an "Intel Core Ultra 100 Series" row (8.21 tok/s) whose chip is not named; issue #8328 (155H, CPU) has only tg256 runs. None is the same chip and test, so the cell stays empty.
gaps.llm|Intel Core Ultra 7 265K: No Llama 2 7B Q4_0 run on this CPU or its Intel Graphics iGPU was found. The machine on this page runs its LLM work on its RTX 4090, which is in the RTX 4090 row.
gaps.llm|Intel Core Ultra 9 275HX: No Llama 2 7B Q4_0 run on this CPU or its Intel Graphics iGPU was found. Its laptops run LLMs on the RTX 5090 Laptop GPU, which is in that row.
gaps.llm|Intel Core 5 320: No Llama 2 7B Q4_0 run was found; the Dell XPS 13 (2026) on this page has only Geerling's Llama 3.2 3B run.
gaps.llm|NVIDIA GeForce RTX 4060: Neither the CUDA nor the Vulkan scoreboard has a desktop RTX 4060 row (only the RTX 4060 Ti, a different chip, and the RTX 4060 Laptop), and no comment with one was found.
gaps.llm|NVIDIA N1X (RTX Spark): No Llama 2 7B Q4_0 run was found: neither the CUDA scoreboard (discussion #15013) nor the Vulkan scoreboard (#10879) has an N1X or RTX Spark row, and no review quotes llama-bench on that model. The GB10 (DGX Spark) rows are a different power envelope and are not relabelled. The N1X's LLM runs on other models (Qwen3 8B, Qwen3.8 27B, Qwen3.6 35B-A3B, gpt-oss 20B and 120B) are on the LLM tab, from n1xllm.py.
gaps.bl-gpu|Intel Core Ultra 7 265K: Open Data has 6 Blender 4.5.0 oneAPI runs of its Intel Graphics iGPU matched by CPU name (372.18 samples/min), but no machine on this page has a wall power with that iGPU loaded: the 265K desktop here has only HPL power, with an RTX 4090 fitted. Its GPU renders on that card are in the RTX 4090 row.
gaps.bl-gpu|Intel Core Ultra 9 275HX: Open Data has 18 Blender 4.5.0 oneAPI runs of its Intel Graphics iGPU matched by CPU name (340.44 samples/min), but no wall power with that iGPU loaded exists for a 275HX machine on this page; its laptops render on the RTX 5090 Laptop GPU, which is in that row.
gaps.bl-gpu|Intel i9-9880H: Its MacBook Pro 16 (2019) renders on the Radeon Pro 5500M: Open Data has Metal runs of that GPU only up to Blender 4.2 (Blender 4.5 dropped Intel Macs), and no wall power under a GPU load exists for this machine on the page (its Cyberpunk cell is empty too), so there is no power to borrow.
gaps.bl-gpu|NVIDIA GB10: Open Data has no GB10 GPU run: its only GB10 entry is one CPU run under Windows on Arm, and the GB10 machines run Linux on Arm, for which Open Data has no launcher.
